I don't even want to give it one star.
I will never go there again.
My dog ​​is a small, elderly dog. I took him there because he was acting as if he couldn't see. Even from an owner's perspective, I don't think he was acting that violently, but he was given a sedative for the examination, then an overdose of steroids, and his condition rapidly deteriorated. The steroids seemed to upset his stomach, and he couldn't eat, and from there, his condition worsened. He ended up being hospitalized at another hospital.

I had heard that this was a top-notch ophthalmologist, and I had been there once before, but I didn't have such a bad impression last time.

The son doctor was constantly arguing with his father. When the father doctor said, "This medicine...", the son doctor would reply, "I just said he's already taking it!", and from an outsider's perspective, it seemed like he was resisting everything the father said.

The examination room on the second floor smelled of cigarettes, the equipment seemed old, and in many ways, it's a past-era renowned doctor that hasn't been updated.

Postscript:
My dog ​​passed away a few weeks later.

I can't determine a direct causal relationship because I haven't performed an autopsy. However, stomach irritation that prevents eating can rapidly worsen a person's health, even in elderly humans. When my father died of cancer, the chemotherapy irritated the mucous membrane of his stomach and intestines, making it impossible for him to eat, and then he passed away very quickly. So I believe this incident may have hastened his death to some extent.

Thinking about this fills me with guilt and regret for not being able to protect him as his owner, and it's something I still want to turn away from.

My beloved dog passed away during an eye examination.

When we took him in because of eye problems, the doctor caused a corneal perforation during eye cleaning.

My dog ​​thrashed about in pain and was muzzled with a bandage.

The bandage was tightened very tightly, and the nurse held him down very firmly, causing him to cry out and lose control of his bladder.

That day, contact lenses were put in, and the procedure was completed successfully, but he seemed unwell all day.

On the follow-up visit, he was again muzzled with a bandage and held down. Whether due to extreme stress, a heart attack, or an arrhythmia (as the head veterinarian suggested), my dog ​​became motionless while being held down and passed away.

He was intubated, received CPR, and injections, but could not be saved.

Up to this point, sudden death can occur in humans as well, so perhaps it's unavoidable.

Afterward, without any angel care for my dog, who was limp and leaking feces, urine, and bodily fluids, I was simply asked, "Do you have a towel?" I was asked what I wanted to do with the body, but they didn't put it in a coffin or anything; they just returned the body to me as is.
I had no choice but to dab it with the towel I had with me.
To top it all off, they probably didn't want other patients to see, so they made me leave through the back door instead of the front.

I used to be a veterinary nurse myself, so I know it's unthinkable for a hospital not to provide angel care for an animal that dies on the premises. It's incredibly rude to the owner, and I can only see it as making a fool of them.
I understand that the ophthalmology department is very busy. But couldn't they at least show some sincerity towards the animal that died during the procedure?

I feel terribly sorry that because I brought my dog ​​to this hospital, she suffered terribly and was scared until the very end, and that she passed away like that.

I was a regular customer, so I believe their ophthalmology skills are solid. I've been a customer many times.

However, as a human being, as someone involved in the animal industry, as a veterinarian, and as a veterinary nurse, I think they are the worst.

I'm writing this review so that no more animals like my dog, who fought so hard but suffered terribly and painfully, will have to go through what we did. My beloved dog will return to heaven tomorrow. She was such a good dog, low-maintenance until the very end.

We will never go back to our house again, but I never imagined that a visit to have her eye treated would result in bringing home her remains.

I want my dog ​​back.

June 2, 2025 Update

The veterinarian who caused the corneal perforation has returned to work.

How dare he shamelessly return to work after killing someone else's beloved dog. He must have no heart. Normally, you wouldn't think of going back to work after killing a former patient's dog, would you?

The doctors are wonderful, and the nurses are incredibly caring and attentive. Every word the doctors speak carries a sense of authority, and the nurses' respectful work ethic is truly a pleasure to witness. My child was truly saved by this hospital.

My dog ​​has atopic dermatitis and we're taking him to Dr. Kudo for treatment.

We'd been to several different hospitals, but his condition wasn't improving, so we started going to Dr. Kudo six months ago. Because he's researched dermatology, he provides very effective prescriptions. He pays attention not only to the skin but also to the dog's mental state, which I think is why we're seeing results so quickly.

Regarding the cost, the consultation fees aren't cheap, but considering the expertise and skill involved, I think they're reasonable, or even slightly inexpensive. Also, while medication needs to be administered in certain amounts over the long term, it's cheaper than other hospitals, making it easier to continue going, and I feel much more at ease entrusting my dog ​​to him.

I lost my sight due to hypertensive retinal detachment, and was referred to you by my family doctor and immediately seen by you. After a thorough examination and accurate diagnosis, I was given medication and was able to see again soon after. Director Kudo was very happy when I was able to see again. I always felt the doctor's strong determination to cure me, which gave me peace of mind. I can really feel his love for animals. I'm a little scared of people, but I think his diagnoses are excellent and accurate. I'm grateful that he saved my life.

The staff are trustworthy.

They never force animals to do anything they don't want to do, and I've never seen any pets get scared.

My Chihuahua is being cared for here. The doctors and staff are kind, so I have no complaints at the moment.
I had my female Chihuahua spayed here, and she is doing well since the surgery.

First of all, the area around the examination room smelled strongly of cigarette smoke, which was quite unpleasant.

Despite charging surprisingly high treatment fees each time (perhaps due to their unique methods?), the treatment itself was no different from other animal hospitals.

They do perform cataract surgery, but I would advise you to hear from multiple owners who have actually had the surgery, and consult with other hospitals before making a decision.

Ultimately, I didn't have the surgery done, and the deciding factors were the information I heard from several people about the physical burden on the dog, the considerable financial burden on the owner, the restrictions on daily life, and the fact that the post-operative results were not as expected. Above all, the numerous unconfident remarks from the head veterinarian and a young, apprentice-like veterinarian were major reasons why I decided against it.

Finally, they have one emergency parking space a short distance away, but they should stop parking ultra-luxury cars in front of the hospital and keep at least one parking space open for emergencies or owners of severely ill dogs.

I can't help but think that the doctors at this hospital don't like animals.
The elderly doctor yells, and the assistant grabs my child tightly, restraining him.
The consultation fees are more than 1.5 times higher than other clinics, abnormally expensive, and they don't provide an itemized bill. (They might provide one now if you ask.)
My child's eyes didn't improve at all.
